article.title: Trump Struggles Against Easy, Hard and Personal Questions
article.author: Julien Hennefeld
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Trump’s amazing brain is well documented. On each of his three short stays in the hospital Trump was given a cognitive exam designed to test for early signs of dementia and cognitive decline. And each time he aced them with a perfect score. The first question typically tested visual perceptiveness, like given pictures of a lion, a giraffe, a bear and a shark, which one was the bear? Not that hard, but the right level of difficulty for Joe Biden. However, later questions were extremely difficult. At a rally, Trump wowed the crowd by revealing one of the harder questions. It involved performing calculations in quick succession without pencil and paper. Here is the question: Pick a number greater than 100, sir. Trump said okay 203. Now, multiply it by 9, Divide by 2, Add 1,324, Subtract 1,292, and finally Multiply by 19. What is your result, sir? Related: How Trump’s Incompetence and Looming Global Catastrophes May Intersect And not surprisingly, Trump immediately gave the correct answer. Predictably, various fake news, low-IQ critics tried to downplay this evidence of Trump's genius brain by insisting that such a difficult question wouldn’t be included in an exam to test for early signs of dementia. However, Trump, not these critics, was the person who actually took the exam. And Trump was able to recall in vivid detail exactly how that question was stated, down to the fact that he was referred to as sir. Trump has an unusual relationship to questions of a philosophical or political nature. For Trump there are basically three categories of such questions. They are questions that are: too easy too hard, even for him just too personal to publicly discuss In light of his super genius brain, some questions that are easy for Trump are objectively extremely hard. However, some questions are so hard that they are even hard for him. A striking example of a too personal question was when Trump boasted that his favorite book was the Bible. When the interviewer politely asked Trump what were some of his favorite verses of the sacred book, Trump declined to name even one. Various fake news commentators have insinuated that this was because Trump was actually unfamiliar with the Bible. However, nothing could be further from the truth. As Trump explained, the Bible was so deeply personal for him that he insisted that his right to keep his thoughts about it private be respected. Sometimes a question which is objectively hard for other people but very easy for him, can also be extremely personal to Trump. A perfect example was when the fake news reporter Kristin Welker said to Trump that he had never provided any evidence to support his accusation that the 2020 election was rigged. She asked Trump to explain how he knew that the election was stolen. This was such a deeply personal issue for Trump because he didn’t want to relive the hurt caused by the nefarious actions of the Democrats. So, using his genius brain, he was able to give a succinct answer which objectively put the matter to rest by saying “all I have to do is look.” End of discussion. The possible calamitous effects of climate change present a potentially difficult problem even for Trump because it is imperative that Trump retain a tight grip on his power. Enacting policies to address climate change would pose an enormous risk to Trump. For example, taking the obvious step of decreasing the emission of greenhouse gases would entail reducing our use of fossil fuels. But this would alienate his billionaire fossil fuel pals. Even worse, it would cause a big spike in prices and inconvenient life style changes for the already aggrieved members of his base. This could cause his base to see Trump as betraying them by caving in to the enemy. How was Trump to resolve this seemingly unsolvable climate change conundrum? I have learned from a White House aide the process that Trump used. He decided to follow in the footsteps of another great genius, namely, Albert Einstein. When Einstein was working on an incredibly complex problem that had baffled physicists for decades, he knew that his only hope for making progress was to manage the complexity by starting out with two simplifying assumptions about the laws of physics and the speed of light that are much too complicated to write here. However, from that starting point of simplifying assumptions, Einstein was able to discover the theory of special relativity. From that theory he deduced the famous equation E=mc 2 , which states that matter and energy were the same entity. A consequence of that equation is that a tiny amount of matter could generate an enormous amount of energy because c was the speed of light and so c squared was a huge number. This equation eventually led to both the atomic bomb and nuclear power plants. To solve the baffling climate change problem, Trump closely followed the reasoning process that Einstein used in discovering the theory of special relativity and deducing the equation E=mc 2 . Given the enormous complexity of the climate change issue, Trump wisely decided that in order to make any progress, a comprehensive simplifying assumption was sorely needed at the outset. And he found exactly the right one. It was both elegant and had far reaching tentacles. Concisely put, Trump’s starting assumption was “that climate change was the greatest con job ever perpetrated on the world.” From this starting framework Trump deductively realized two essential goals. First, it meant that no sacrifices or changes were needed to address the possibility of climate change. Secondly, it had the added benefit of riling up his base who loved having additional reasons to despise the elitist, left-wing environmentalists bent on taking away our freedoms.
